theme: The question is for the parent, not about them. When a morning looks different, Kettle asks him first, quietly, before the family hears a thing.

posts.text: I didn't want something that watches my parents and reports back. I wanted something that asks them first, quietly, before I ever hear a thing. That's the whole idea behind Kettle.

posts.title: Why Kettle asks the parent first, not the family
posts.text:
Why Kettle asks the parent first, not the family

When a morning doesn't look like his own, Kettle sends one quiet question to him, not a report to everyone else. Only if he doesn't answer does the family hear anything at all.
posts.alt: Three-panel comic strip stacked: Walt plays chess on the porch with his phone screen-down beside the board, the phone lights up plainly on the table, and he glances at it before returning to the game. Captions: He gets asked first. One quiet question, just for him. The family hears from us only if he doesn't answer.
posts.note: Self-check: no banned words, no verdict, no em dash, no kinship/culture words, no medical claim, no invented stat, Walt shown capable and busy with his own game throughout, no CTA, link is the brand home rather than a guessed URL.

posts.title: Ask them, don't watch them

script.say: My parents are a long flight away. For a while I thought I wanted updates on them.
script.overlay: I used to want updates on them
script.broll: Founder face to camera, kitchen counter behind him.

script.say: Now I want them asked, not watched. If a morning looks different, Kettle asks my parent first, quietly.
script.broll: Founder face to camera, thoughtful pause.

script.say: Only if they don't answer does our family hear anything at all.
script.overlay: Only then does the family hear
script.broll: Neutral b-roll: a plain phone face down on a kitchen table, no app visible, morning light.

script.say: That's the whole idea. Ask first.
script.broll: Founder face to camera, small smile, kettle visible on the counter behind him.

posts.alt: Cover image: Walt sits at his workbench in warm evening light, his phone lit face up beside him, going about his own business. Caption: Ask them. Don't watch them.

posts.title: Three things, nothing else

script.say: Kettle keeps three things about my parents. Who. Which normal routine. When.
script.broll: Founder face to camera, kitchen counter behind him.

script.say: Not what they said on the phone. Not who they called. Not where they went.
script.overlay: Not what was said or where they went.

script.say: Just that today looked like their day, noticed on the phone they already carry.
script.overlay: Just that today looked like their day.

posts.title: A device you already have, one quiet fact
posts.text:
A device you already have, one quiet fact

A smart plug, a door sensor, or a voice routine already in a parent's home can tell Kettle the time it fired, like Plug, 8:05 this morning. Nothing more. Kettle decides nothing from it.
